carbon_policy_signal.item: COP31 draft text signals immediate fossil fuel transition language; final outcome will determine investor risk premium on legacy coal/gas power infrastructure and EUA long-curve pricing.
carbon_policy_signal.why_it_matters: If finalized with strong fossil-transition clause, heightens EU decarbonization credibility and raises marginal cost of unabated coal dispatch; supports EUA floor and accelerates power-to-renewable substitution merit-order shift.

freshness_caveat: Coal (328 days old, as_of 2025-12-26) and Clean Dark (323 days old, as_of 2025-12-31) are stale; reliance on these metrics for intraday trading decisions is not recommended. All other snapshots are current (≤2 days).
risk_flags: Storage 69.95% (18pp below 5-yr seasonal) — refill pace into winter 2026–27 is critical; <65% would force demand destruction.
Renewables at 78.88% (95th-pctile) suppress DA spreads today; reversion risk if winter weather turns dry.
Russia Arctic LNG (~10% global supply) cut from EU 2027 — reroute to Asia widens LNG transport arbitrage, supports TTF structurally but introduces geopolitical timeline execution risk.
EUA -4.54% yesterday (4.7σ) on COP31 stall — fossil-transition text outcome critical; long-dated EUA curve vulnerable to negotiation breakdown.

base.summary: Renewables sustain 90th+; storage drifts 1–2pp lower; TTF ranges 78–83 EUR/MWh.

downside.summary: Renewables sustain 95th; mild weather reduces storage drawdown; US LNG export surge widens arb. TTF softens on oversupply signal.

upside.summary: Cold front drives storage drawdown acceleration to 65%; renewables revert to 50th-pctile; LNG call lifts. TTF rallies on supply tightness.

themes: Renewables-driven DA compression vs. tight storage refill
Russia LNG sanctions tighten medium-term European gas supply
Coal at 8th-percentile; clean dark spread neutral — fuel switch regime dormant
COP31 fossil-fuel transition language signals long-term EUA support
top_drivers: Renewables at 95th-pctile (78.88% of load) drive DA power collapse and compress front spreads; mean reversion to 40–50% would flip the regime.
Storage 18pp below seasonal (69.95%) tightens winter 2026–27 refill urgency; any demand spike or supply loss forces LNG call or rationing into TTF.
Russia Arctic LNG ban from 2027 removes ~10% of global supply from EU, reroutes to Asia, widens LNG transport arb, and structurally supports TTF via supply tightness.
top_takeaway: Renewables at 95th-percentile suppress DA power; storage 18pp below seasonal normal tightens H2 outlook; Russia Arctic LNG ban from 2027 supports TTF via supply loss.

watchlist.metric: COP31 final text — fossil-fuel transition clause
watchlist.why: Determines investor risk premium on legacy coal/gas; EUA long-curve pricing hinge. Failure to include strong language eases near-term power decarbonization pressure.

watchlist.metric: EU Storage refill velocity through Dec 2026
watchlist.why: At 69.95% and 18pp below seasonal, any demand shock or supply outage into winter 2026–27 forces LNG call or rationing. Daily tracking of storage net withdrawal/injection critical.

watchlist.metric: Russia Arctic LNG sanctions enforcement timeline Jan 2027
watchlist.why: Current news signals 2027 start date; delays or carve-outs would weaken TTF support narrative. Logistics and third-party insurance scrutiny will reveal true enforcement tightness.

watchlist.metric: US LNG export margin and TTF arb strength
watchlist.why: US storage 2% above 5-yr average reduces winter export urgency; weakens Henry Hub→TTF arb and limits downward TTF pressure. Monitor competing bids into NW Europe.
Current 95th-pctile (78.88%) is structural tail; any shift to median (40–50%) would lift DA power price by 15–25% and tighten spark spreads.
